questions.stem: What endocrine effect does long-term morphine have in opioid-dependent patients?
options: Adrenal atrophy with raised corticosteroid secretion
Adrenal hypertrophy with impaired corticosteroid secretion
Thyroid enlargement with raised thyroxine output
Pituitary suppression with raised prolactin levels

questions.stem: How should opioid-dependent patients be premedicated before anaesthesia?
options: Premedication withheld to avoid respiratory depression
Benzodiazepine alone, with no opioid
Adequate premedication with opioids
Minimal premedication with an antiemetic only

questions.stem: What should opioid-dependent patients receive during and after surgery, beyond their premedication?
options: Extra opioid intraoperatively and postoperatively
Usual opioid dose only, none given during surgery
Opioids withheld until the patient is awake
Strictly opioid-free care with no postoperative opioid

questions.stem: Which additional analgesia is advised for opioid-dependent patients?
options: Oral codeine as the sole analgesic
Higher-dose opioid infusion alone
Intrathecal morphine only
Non-opioid analgesics and nerve blocks

questions.stem: Is there an ideal anaesthetic agent or technique for opioid-dependent patients, and what role do antagonists have?
questions.answer: No ideal agent or technique; an opioid antagonist may be used judiciously where indicated

questions.stem: Which adjuncts work well with regional anaesthesia in opioid-dependent patients?
options: High-dose ketamine and propofol infusion
Low-dose ketamine and α2-agonists
Pethidine and metoclopramide
Nitrous oxide and midazolam infusion

questions.stem: What circulatory support and monitoring are advised for opioid-dependent patients?
options: Fluids for circulation, with arterial blood gases and respiratory monitoring
Fluid restriction, with pulse oximetry only
Colloid bolus only, with no respiratory monitoring
Vasopressor first, with no blood gas checks
